title: Dynamic Model Routing
summary: Select an eligible model for each task using measured capability, quality, latency, and cost while keeping policy constraints mandatory.
overview: Dynamic model routing chooses among models according to the request rather than sending all work to one default. A router may consider task type, input modality, context length, required tools, latency deadline, and evaluated difficulty. Cost and latency are optimization objectives only after the model satisfies the task and data-policy contract.

Routing introduces its own error surface. A cheap classifier can underestimate a difficult request, while a complex router can cost more than it saves. Model self-confidence is not a reliable universal complexity score. Start with transparent rules, collect outcome data, and add learned routing only when the evaluation supports it.

production.poc: A prototype compares a fixed strong baseline with a simple two-route policy on labeled tasks.
production.production: Production versions routing decisions, evaluates each route, and defines escalation when output validation fails.
production.scale: Enterprise scale handles capacity, regional eligibility, tenant budgets, and drift while keeping routing changes independently reversible from model changes.

components.name: Request profiler
components.role: Extracts task requirements and bounded complexity signals.

components.name: Capability registry
components.role: Records approved modalities, schemas, regions, and evaluated quality.

components.name: Routing policy
components.role: Chooses the lowest-cost eligible route meeting the service objective.

components.name: Outcome validator
components.role: Checks task-specific acceptance and triggers permitted escalation.

components.name: Decision ledger
components.role: Stores route version, selected model, reasons, and actual usage.

flow.title: Resolve hard constraints
flow.description: Determine data location, required features, and maximum context before optimizing cost.

flow.title: Profile task difficulty
flow.description: Use observable request features and evaluated heuristics rather than ungrounded confidence.

flow.title: Select eligible route
flow.description: Combine capability, current capacity, and the task’s quality floor.

flow.title: Execute and validate
flow.description: Run inference and check schema, evidence, or business acceptance rules.

flow.title: Escalate selectively
flow.description: Use a stronger approved route only when the remaining deadline and budget permit.

flow.title: Learn from outcomes
flow.description: Compare route-level quality and total cost, including classifier and escalation overhead.

useCase.title: Routing routine and unusual correspondence
useCase.situation: A service assistant classifies routine claim correspondence and drafts explanations for unusual disputes.
useCase.problem: Using one large model for every label is costly, while a small model struggles with complex exceptions.
useCase.requirement: Route routine classification efficiently and reserve stronger reasoning for exception-heavy tasks.
useCase.architecture: A task profiler selects evaluated model routes and a validator checks classification schema and evidence requirements.
runtime: A standard document label uses the specialized route.
An ambiguous dispute with several policy references uses the stronger route or escalates after validation failure.
useCase.failure: If the router version begins underclassifying difficult cases, traffic returns to the fixed baseline while the routing policy is reviewed.
useCase.impact: Measure accepted-task cost, escalation rate, and quality by route; nominal per-token savings can disappear after repeated failures.

tradeoffs.benefit: Are explainable and cheap to operate.

tradeoffs.cost: Needs labels, monitoring, and its own rollout controls.
Adds latency and may pay for two generations.

failures.detection: One route shows rising validation failures.
failures.recovery: Tighten eligibility and revert affected tasks to the baseline.

failures.detection: Selected endpoints throttle despite good quality fit.
failures.recovery: Include live capacity and bounded fallback behavior.

mistakes.fix: Compare total cost per accepted task.
Use calibrated outcomes and observable features.
Apply hard eligibility constraints before selection.

whenToUse: Use for mixed workloads with distinct capability needs.
Use when route quality can be evaluated by task class.
Use when cost savings exceed routing and escalation overhead.
whenNotToUse: Avoid complex routing for uniform low-volume work.
Do not route sensitive data to unapproved models.
Avoid unvalidated difficulty classifiers for consequential tasks.
